And I'd especially like to point out to the Trial Chamber the fact that General Lazarevic insisted in Exhibit PD365 [as interpreted], points 3, 4, and 5, that the subordinate units -- he demanded that the subordinate units provide for the unimpeded engagement and work of the military investigating organs and the judiciary, and that all members of the corps should adhere strictly to international humanitarian law and all the orders of the Pristina Corps to date. In the same order, it is requested that help be provided for the return of displaced persons; P2029, point 4 also indicates this. It should also be stressed, and this can be seen from P1306, that General Lazarevic issued a special order demanding that in all units of the Pristina Corps, Special Forces be formed to look after the civilian population, and they are ordered to find out the numbers of displaced civilians in the areas where the units are deployed in order to provide sufficient foodstuffs for the population and other necessities of life. That's P1306. And to avoid repetition, there are numerous exhibits showing that General Lazarevic was careful to ensure that his units treated civilians humanely, and that they returned them to the villages and towns from which they had been displaced. And I wish to draw Your Honours' attention to 5D372, where General Lazarevic orders his subordinate units, and I quote that: "The return of the civilian population to their towns and villages from which they had moved out should be speeded up." He asks the brigade commanders not to allow the civilian population to be in places where refugees gather, but that they should be returned to the places from which they had fled. So he is not carrying out a plan to expel them; on the contrary, he's demanding that civilians be returned to the towns and villages from which they had fled due to the fighting. There is numerous evidence also which this Defence has tried to show were not just something on paper, that the subordinate units actually did implement these orders, and that they reported to General Lazarevic about the way in which his orders were being implemented. And, finally, let me say that all the exhibits we have mentioned indicate that the accused General Lazarevic legitimately believed and had reason to believe that as the corps commander, he was fighting to preserve the sovereignty and integrity of his country, and the most impressive piece of evidence for this assertion for the Defence was provided by the Prosecutor, in fact. The Prosecution office which brought an insider witness from the VJ, K-73, who said that General Lazarevic was someone all the officers thought highly of, that they considered him a professional soldier, a good, honest, and honourable man, and a strong commander. In the opinion of this witness, General Lazarevic was never a politician or a careerist. He was a military leader, a soldier who was defending his country. Let me remind Your Honours that this witness asked the Chamber for permission to address General Lazarevic directly; and on that occasion, he said that it had been an honour for him to serve his country under the command of General Lazarevic. Your Honours, bearing in mind all the evidence to which the Defence has pointed in its closing arguments and final brief, we propose and we move that the Trial Chamber acquit General Lazarevic of all responsibility in relation to all the counts of the indictment. Thank you, Your Honours, for allowing me extra time for my closing arguments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, do you envisage asking to address us further?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have you any idea of the extent of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll try to be very short because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I'm not asking you to be very short. I'm just asking you if you can give me some guidance on what you envisage.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, right now, in light of what's been said, maybe an hour, and there may be some more after Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. And be clear that we do wish you to address anything that you feel, in light of all that's been said, ought to be drawn to our attention without having too close regard to the issue of timing at this late stage in the proceedings. We have to adjourn now and that will have to be until tomorrow, I'm afraid, because I'm told all the courtrooms will be fully occupied this afternoon. Tomorrow, the sitting time is 2.15. If at a reasonable time we were to discover that the morning was available, then you would be notified in the hope that we could re-arrange things; but as presently advised, that is unlikely and therefore we adjourn now until 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 26th day of August, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: [The Accused Pavkovic and Lazarevic not present]
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.48 a.m.,
